recipes.name: Sausage inspired by God of War
ingredients: 1 kilo wild boar meat, cut into one inch cubes
100 g fat back or pork belly, cut into half inch cubes
1/4 cup chicken stock, more as needed
3 tsp freshly ground black pepper, as needed
instructions: For the Ground Meat
Place all grinder pieces on a baking sheet and transfer to the freezer.

Line a second baking sheet with parchment paper and spread the cubed wild boar meat and pork fat evenly on the prepared sheet. - 1 kilo wild boar meat cut into one inch cubes - 100 g fat back or pork belly cut into half inch cubes
Freeze for 20-30 minutes, or until very firm, but not frozen solid.
While the meat is freezing, add hog casings to a large mixing bowl and soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain, then flush casings with fresh water and set aside until ready to use. - hog casings

Set up the grinder with the medium coarse die and pass the meat and fat through, grinding the mixture into a large bowl. Then cover. - wild boar meat cut into one inch cubes - fat back or pork belly cut into half inch cubes
Transfer ground meat to the refrigerator while you prepare the spice mix. - For the Ground Meat
For the Spice Mix
Quarter and grate white onion and transfer to a medium mixing bowl. - ¼ large white onion grated

In the same bowl, add kosher salt, nutmeg, ground clove, black pepper, and stock. Mix to combine. - 3 tsp kosher salt - ¾ tsp freshly grated nutmeg - ½ tsp ground clove - 3 tsp freshly ground black pepper as needed - ¼ cup chicken stock more as needed
For the Sausage
Then, add spice mix to ground meat, using your hands to gently combine the two mixtures together. - Spice Mix - Ground Meat
Add additional stock if the mixture seems too dry. It needs to be soft, but not loose. - chicken stock more as needed
Once mixed, fry a small patty in a skillet to taste for seasoning and adjust as needed. - For the Ground Meat
After the sausage mixture is to your liking, prepare your sausage stuffer with casing, tying and poking a hole in the end. - hog casings - For the Sausage
Stuff into the casing, creating one long ring of sausage. This is typically a 2 person job, but it’s better to under-stuff the sausage casing than over-stuff.

Make sure the sausage meat is evenly distributed throughout the casing and just firm, coil the assembled sausage, and poke small holes in the casing every 5 cm to prevent blowout during the cooking process. - For the Sausage
For the Smoking
Place the assembled sausage coil on a parchment lined baking sheet and refrigerate while you set up your fire. - For the Sausage

Build a small fire and create direct and indirect heat zones. Place the sausage in the indirect heat, and aim for the temperature to always be between 130°-160°F. If the fire becomes too hot, move the sausage as far away from the heat source as possible. Place a small aluminum pan filled with water next to the sausage. Cover with a large metal bowl and smoke until the internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove sausage and transfer to a wire racked sheet tray. - For the Sausage
Transfer to the refrigerator and allow to cool completely. When ready to eat, reheat over the fire or on the grill. - For the Sausage
Serve alongside lager and boiled potatoes. Or your choice of drink and veggies.
